svg.title: Analyst: journey through the playbook
svg.desc: Nine stops, from the question you were handed to the lessons you leave behind.

div.span: Nine stops, from the question you were handed to the lessons you leave behind.

div.b: 1. You have been asked to do a piece of analysis
2. Is this the question they meant to ask?
3. How much assurance does this need?
4. What do I actually have to do?
5. What do I not know, and how much does it matter?
6. Someone independent needs to check this
7. How do I write this up without overclaiming?
8. Is any of this ethically or legally loaded?

div.span:
R11
Data ethics and personal data

div.div: Take the short path: decide your level, then find what it requires.
Agree the decision, the question, what is out of scope, the deadline.
Score impact and likelihood with your commissioner. Take the highest of each.
Read the block for your level and the blocks inside it.
Find the principal sources of uncertainty while design can still change.
Your own verification and validation first, then the critical friend.
State the caveats in the output itself, not only in an annex.
Check the Data and AI Ethics Framework, personal data and transparency scope.
Ask whether it worked, and whether it is still right.

div.span: The evidence trail, read on its own

div.div: Nothing recorded yet.
The scope and specification, with the question in one sentence.
The assurance level decision sheet, with the Business Critical answer either way.
The quality assurance checklist, and your reviewer's time in the schedule.
Assumptions listed with their rationale and the impact if wrong.
The quality assurance log, and what you did about each finding.
The output and the quality assurance statement, published from Level 3.
The ethics position recorded, and a transparency record drafted where in scope.
The review record, the lessons, and any decommissioning decision.

div.span: What the playbook warns about here

div.div: Challenging a brief is part of the job.
At scoping and not later. About five minutes.
The checks are cumulative. Name your reviewer before you start.
No agreed margin of error means no threshold to test against.
A checklist shows intent. A log shows it was done.
Ask information governance before the work starts, not at sign-off.
At Level 1 the review is yours to own.

Any one impact
dimension at 4?

Yes. The work is Business Critical. Business Critical analysis is the route in nine steps, and it brings Level 4 BCA, a register entry and a named Analysis Senior Responsible Officer, all starting at scoping. Everything else on this journey still applies.

div.span: Stop 9 loops back to stop 2. What you record at the end is what the next piece of work starts from.
Open alongside, at any stop. R8 for which standards bind this work. Roles and responsibilities for who owns a decision you are stuck on. R2 for the template. R3 for the person.
NHSBSA Producing Quality Analysis Playbook. Service design artefacts for workshop use. Kainos Software Limited, SOW-DOC053.
